name: BAHRAIN

flag.title: Flag of Bahrain
flag.note: White and serrated red, 5 white points

lead: Bahrain is a tiny island kingdom in the Persian Gulf, smaller than London. Pearl divers worked its warm waters for thousands of years. Bahrain was the first Gulf country to strike oil. When the oil began to run out, it built racing circuits and banks.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Bahrain is 33 islands in a shallow bay between Qatar and Saudi Arabia. A causeway almost 25 km long joins it to Saudi Arabia.
Most land is flat and sandy. Freshwater springs bubble up from the seabed, and ancient sailors prized them. Springs also feed date palms in the north.
animals: The Arabian oryx roams a protected reserve. Bottlenose dolphins loop through the shallow Gulf. At night, hawksbill turtles crawl up quiet beaches to lay eggs.
The Hawar Islands hold one of the world's largest nesting colonies of Socotra cormorants. The dugong, a gentle sea-cow, grazes on seagrass.
culture: Bahrainis love the majlis, where people sip cardamom coffee and talk for hours. Sawt music, played on the oud lute, drifts from open doors.
The Bahrain Grand Prix roars through Sakhir each year. People feast on machboos, spiced rice with fish or lamb. Ramadan evenings become street festivals.
history: Bahrain was the heart of ancient Dilmun, a trading land named in Sumerian texts 5,000 years ago. The Portuguese captured its forts in 1521. The Al Khalifa family, who rule today, arrived in 1783.
Britain made Bahrain a protectorate in 1820. Oil came in 1932, then independence in 1971. As oil ran low, Bahrain became a banking hub.
wows: Bahrain has more cars per km of road than almost anywhere.
The 400-year-old Tree of Life grows alone in the desert.
Over 100,000 ancient burial mounds once dotted the island.
In 2002, Bahrain was the Gulf's first country where women voted and ran for office.
Bahrain means 'two seas', for fresh and salt water mixing around the islands.
Japan's cultured pearls wiped out Bahrain's pearl trade in the 1930s.
The Bahrain Grand Prix races at night under bright floodlights.

myths.fact: Pearls grow inside oysters. A tiny speck gets in, and the oyster coats it with shiny layers.

myths.myth: Bahrain is too hot to visit
myths.fact: From November to March, days are mild at about 15–25 °C.
